name: Itata Valley
shape: Chile Decreto 464, drawn from its comunas and provinces

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Riesling, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

soil.rock: Granite weathers to coarse, acid, free-draining soil that warms quickly and holds heat. Its acidity tends to lower the grapes' acidity, which suits Gamay.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
